guidelineReference: SJA First Aid / minor wound care
title: Minor graze at a park event
setting: Park event. 22F fainted briefly, now alert, with a small graze on her arm from falling off a bicycle at low speed. Walking and talking normally.
verdictExplanation: Alert, fully responsive, stable observations. A minor superficial graze with negligible bleeding and no systemic symptoms. Not sick: simple wound care.

shared.circulation: Minor graze on left forearm, slight bleeding

history.history: Slipped off bike on a gravel path moments ago, fainted briefly but recovered immediately
history.drugs: GTN spray (has not needed to use it today)
history.additional: Had a minor heart attack a year ago but currently completely pain-free and well

followUp.question: What is the correct protocol for managing this minor graze?

options.text: Clean the wound with water or alcohol-free wipes, dry, and apply a plaster
Apply a tourniquet above the elbow to prevent infection
Administer the patient's GTN spray immediately as a precaution
Call 999 due to the patient's cardiac history

followUp.explanation: Superficial grazes require simple cleaning and dressing to prevent infection. Tourniquets are for life-threatening haemorrhage. GTN is only for cardiac chest pain. 999 is not indicated as she is stable and symptom-free.

levelFlags.cfaNotes: Clean and dress the graze. Ask about tetanus status.
levelFlags.erNotes: Reassure, check tetanus status, advise on wound hygiene, and safety-net for signs of infection.
